write_policy.rule: All non-production AgentOS development must explicitly target the integration branch or a declared short-lived child branch. Never omit branch on GitHub write operations.

active_work.goal: Complete AgentOS Core v0.1 as the canonical cross-session execution path and prove its execution plane is independent from GitHub Actions: durable context, scoped clients, bounded Oracle-native capabilities, receipts, and a weak-executor Master Experience Floor must remain system-owned.
current_findings: Oracle runs persistent agentos-control-plane.service and agentos-node.service; the native node leases Canonical IR tasks and completes receipts without GitHub Actions being the executor.
Session A -> task -> Oracle execution -> receipt -> Session B attach continuity is proven against the durable Control Plane store.
The public ONE/Core network edge is proven from an external client using short-lived scoped AgentOS credentials; test credentials are revoked after each proof.
Client credentials are stored only as SHA-256 digests and support expiry, revocation, permissions, project allowlists, and capability allowlists; runtime lease/complete APIs remain root-only.
agentos.project.inspect is a native allowlisted capability; LeopardCat inspection returned HEAD f44db405678cd54ce42b944e71a37de033ed8234 from executor oracle-core-node.
agentos.project.test is a native profile-gated capability; task-supplied argv/command fields are ignored in favor of the Oracle-local administrator registry.

The external least-privilege native-test proof succeeded: a token restricted to agentos-core + agentos.project.test submitted core-v01 over the public Core edge, received an oracle-core-node succeeded receipt, was denied cross-project and cross-capability access, and was then revoked.
Context Compiler v0 is deterministic rather than model-generated. /v1/attach returns agentos.execution-context/v0.1 with active goal, findings, next actions, latest task, branch and write policy.
A blind fresh-session attach with history=none recovered the updated canonical Core v0.1 goal and next action using durable context alone.

Execution context exposes a freshness contract with source_updated_at, compiled_at, age_seconds, max_age_seconds and fresh/stale/unknown status; stale context remains visible rather than silently trusted.

Claude Code 2.1.246 invoked as a standalone Antigravity extension binary times out at 25 seconds even in an empty workspace with --bare, tools disabled, dontAsk and low effort. Launching the same binary through the ubuntu systemd user manager also times out, so SSH environment differences alone do not explain the failure.

Process/IPC metadata proves the timed-out standalone Claude process is outside the live Antigravity extension-host process tree. The live Antigravity node tree owns multiple vscode-ipc sockets and the same-user Codex router at ~/.codex/ipc/ipc.sock.

The official Codex app-server surface works immediately from the same Oracle noninteractive environment: codex-cli 0.150.0-alpha.8 completed initialize and model/list without a user turn or filesystem mutation.

The Oracle Codex model catalog currently exposes six visible models. The weakest visible model is gpt-5.4-mini and its minimum advertised reasoning effort is low; this is now the canonical weak-executor candidate rather than an assumed model setting.

WorkspaceGuard and the bounded Antigravity relay remain relevant for interactive/local executor integration, but the standalone Claude CLI is not currently a validated authorized Antigravity session surface and must not be treated as one.
feature/distributed-agentos-runtime remains the sole canonical vNext continuation line; experimental writes to main remain denied.
next_actions: Run a blind fresh-session Master Experience Floor probe on the officially available gpt-5.4-mini + low combination through Codex app-server. Give it only the current /v1/attach execution_context, use an ephemeral read-only thread with approvals disabled, and verify goal, current position, next action, governance boundary and autonomous continuation intent.

If the weak probe passes, implement a bounded Codex app-server executor adapter that consumes AgentOS execution_context and returns a structured receipt including model, reasoning effort, thread/turn identity and evaluation evidence; do not depend on the private vscode-ipc protocol.
Add automatic canonical-context reconciliation/checkpoint rules so successful receipts can advance durable development context without relying on manual summary maintenance.

Separate CI/deployment responsibilities from the normal AgentOS execution plane in repository contracts and workflows, then preserve evidence that deployed Core services and Oracle task execution do not depend on a running GitHub Actions job.
Preserve the Core v0.1 and weak-executor evidence in the AgentOS research chronology, update the paper, and isolate or retire legacy workflows that still fail noisily on every branch push.
